Fresh Daily puzzles. No ads. No subscriptions. No Wi-Fi needed.

title: Brainclash
summary: New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you. Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime. Questions span a wide range of categories — General Knowledge, Science & Nature, History, Geography, Sports, and Arts & Entertainment — so you'll always find something that suits your interests and adds to what you know. And when a hard question comes your way, you have tools to help: remove half the options with 50:50, swap a question that doesn't suit you, or grant yourself a few extra seconds. The more you win, the higher you climb through the levels and the more coins you collect — and each day you can spin the daily wheel for a free reward. The game is made for everyone to enjoy: it works smoothly with TalkBack and VoiceOver, so screen reader users get a complete experience, crafted to be heard and not only seen. Add your friends, exchange messages between matches, and discover together who deserves the title of the smartest. Play in Arabic or English, and switch languages whenever you wish. So, are you ready to compete? Your next opponent is waiting on your move. Heading

title: ‎Muse from Meta
summary: Muse is a personal AI agent that can manage email and schedules, book reservations, track spending, compare prices, plan workouts, and handle multistep tasks. It can connect to apps you choose, keep working after you close it, and ask for approval before taking actions. You can interact with Muse either through the native iOS app, through a browser interface at http://muse.ai or through WhatsApp chat messages. Includes a robust free tier, and optional paid subscriptions if you go over.

title: Earcade
summary: Earcade is a collection of nine audio-only games for blind and low vision players. Every game is played entirely by ear; no visual information is required at any point. The games use binaural HRTF spatial audio, so the position and movement of objects is conveyed through where sounds appear around you. Headphones are recommended. Haptic feedback is used alongside audio in most of the games. Menus and navigation are built for VoiceOver. The app is free, has no ads, and no gameplay content is locked behind a purchase. There is an optional tip jar which unlocks nothing.

title: Final Fortress
summary: Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress. It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it. Match tiles to finish the day's tasks. Each task brings supplies. Spend them to repair the fortress: reactor, hydroponics, antenna, armory, infirmary. Every repaired system opens new missions. Match 4 or more to charge special tiles. They clear a line, a block, or every tile of one kind. Swap two charged tiles together and they fire as one bigger shape, up to the whole board. The board gets busier as you go: convoy crates that pay out at the bottom, sealed containers with a special tile inside, interference to clear layer by layer, burned sectors the tiles fall past. Some tasks ask for a pattern: decode a sequence in order, or fill a gauge in every column. AI Madness is a mode of its own, outside the fortress. Each shift bends the rules: boards up to 10 by 13, sometimes only three kinds of tile, cascades that barely stop, tasks that may be impossible. On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, Apple's on-device model (Foundation Models) picks the shift's character and writes its line in the log. Nothing leaves the phone. Otherwise the terminal does the same on its own. Nothing is at stake and nothing is banked. Every shift has a code. Send it to a friend and they get exactly the same board. There is a story in the log: three acts, four threads, and the notes of the commandants who held the fortress before you. It comes a few lines at a time. Read it or skip it. The game never nags about it. Repair the antenna and you will see a board with other players' stations. It is view-only, there is no chat, and it updates once a day. When the story is over, the log keeps going quietly on its own. The music belongs to your fortress alone. The sound is synthesized live and seeded from your fortress, so your station hums like no other and never loops. The hum changes with what is running, with the hour of the night and with the weather outside. Each kind of tile has its own note, and a cascade climbs the scale. One extra room, The Long Dark, carries a call of its own. Three more stations use the instruments in your phone: a weather post that reads the barometer, an acoustic modem and a direction finder. A home screen widget shows your fortress at a glance, in StandBy too. No ads. No lives, timers, energy or streaks. No pop-ups, no push notifications, no accounts, no daily rewards to come back for. Run out of moves and the terminal just says the packet was lost. Try again, nothing is taken away. You can drop a task at any time. Purchases are cosmetic only: screen colors, one extra soundtrack, custom names. Nothing you can buy helps you play, and no purchase moves you up the board. Works offline, on iPhone and iPad. Fully playable with VoiceOver, with a flicker-free stable phosphor mode and a calm mode that softens the board's flashes and haptics.

title: One Line Journal app
summary: One sentence a day. One book at the end of the year. Your life is happening — quietly, quickly, in small moments. One Line, One Year captures 2026 as it unfolds and turns it into a beautifully structured book that's entirely yours. HOW IT WORKS Daily — Write one sentence about your day. That's it. Weekly — Once a week, reflect in 3–5 sentences. Your daily entries appear above for context, so nothing gets lost. Monthly — Write a brief summary that becomes a full chapter in your book. Book View — Watch your year assemble itself in real time — months as chapters, weeks and days woven beneath them. Export — At year's end, export your complete book as Markdown, PDF, or DOCX. BUILT FOR PRIVACY Everything stays on your device. No accounts. No cloud sync. No analytics. Face ID and passcode lock keep your words yours — and auto-lock kicks in the moment you leave the app. THOUGHTFUL DETAILS Highlights to mark the moments worth remembering Tags to thread themes across your year Gentle reminders to keep the habit alive A clean, distraction-free writing interface Simple timeline navigation — no clutter, no feed NO SOCIAL. NO NOTIFICATIONS. NO NOISE. Just you and your words, building something you'll want to read. A year feels long while you're living it. It feels short when you look back. Capture it — one sentence at a time.

title: Idle Dyson Swarm
summary: Build an automated solar empire from a single bot into a galaxy-spanning Dyson swarm. Create bots, manufacture solar panels, harness stars for energy, and reinvest your profits into an ever-growing production network. Idle Dyson Swarm expands far beyond the first star: • Unlock Research, Skills, Facilities and Mega-Structures • Break through Infinity and optimise repeated prestige runs • Explore Simulations, Reality and Quantum progression • Process offline progress with configurable Stored Time controls • Inspect detailed production formulas and performance statistics • Customise navigation, number notation, audio and processing speed • Continue an existing same-device save from the original Unity version Play in English, French, German, Latin American Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Russian or Japanese. Progress at your own pace, refine your automation, and see how much of reality your swarm can consume.

title: Remote Incident Manager Mobile
summary: Harness the power of born-accessible remote desktop, right in the palm of your hand! Remote Incident Manager’s mobile companion turns your iPhone or iPad into a powerful universal remote for any PC or Mac running Remote Incident Manager, opening up a world of possibilities. Tap into your home computer while on your commute, and control it as if you were right there in front of it! Run full support or training sessions straight from your phone, complete with crystal-clear voice conversations. Perform routine maintenance on machines across fleets, anytime, anywhere! All this and more with just a phone and a keyboard! Features: Accessible by design. Simple by nature. Near-complete keyboard control across Windows and macOS, irrespective of screen reader. Accessible, customizable touch keyboard and VoiceOver gesture-based control, making simple tasks possible in the absence of a keyboard. High-fidelity, low-latency audio output from the remote computer. Clear visual output with precise mouse/trackpad control. Crystal-clear voice conversations with built-in noise cancelation. In-session text chat capability. No screen reader? No problem! Leverage our Remote Accessibility module to provide assistance to a computer without the need to install a screen reader! Secure peer-to-peer connections between your phone and a remote computer make for extremely low latency (even on mobile data!). Note: This mobile companion is designed solely as a controller and cannot be used as a target. In other words, a computer cannot control a phone running the companion. Account registration through the desktop client or Remote Incident Manager website prior to your first use of this app is highly recommended for an optimal experience.

title: ghostWriter Markdown
summary: Accessibility-first Markdown writing with VoiceOver-friendly editing, document organization, and flexible exports to Word, PDF, HTML, braille, and more. ghostWriter Markdown is a plain-text writing app for notes, articles, lists, documentation, and anything else you want to say with words. It was built accessibility-first. Not accessibility-eventually, or accessibility-in-the-settings-somewhere. VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code, as the app has been fully created by a Blind developer. If you write with a screen reader, this app was made for you. If you don't, you get a clean, fast, native editor that never gets in your way. So what's Markdown? Markdown adds structure to writing using a few ordinary punctuation marks. A number sign makes a heading. A dash makes a list item. Your document stays readable as plain text, and you can render it whenever you want to see the finished formatting. You don't have to know any of this to start. The Insert feature can add common elements for you, and a built-in Markdown Reference is always a tap away. Writing Made Easy: • A native editor with the Markdown punctuation kept visible, so you always control the source • Insert Actions for links, images, headings, quotes, code, lists, tasks, tables, and rules • Automatic list continuation for bullets, numbers, and task lists • Indent and outdent with tabs or spaces, your choice • Find and Replace, dictation, braille input, and text selection through native iOS controls • A configurable Status Bar showing line, column, word count, current heading, and selection • Automatic saving as you pause, plus Save Now whenever you want it Useful Navigation: • Outline lists every heading in your document and jumps straight to one, moving both the cursor and VoiceOver focus • A 3-finger horizontal swipe with VoiceOver will move the cursor through your document headings while editing • Jump to Line for long documents • Search across document names and their contents • Your last editing position is remembered in every file Keep Files Organized: • Nested folders you can create, rename, move, and navigate • Pin the documents you keep coming back to • Sort by name, created, modified, or last opened • Recently Deleted holds removed files until you restore them or clear them out • Import Markdown, .txt, Word .docx or Powerpoint presentations to convert them into Markdown Render and Share: • See your Markdown as structured HTML right inside the app • Share complete standalone HTML, Markdown, plain text, ePub, tagged PDF, eBraille, BRF, Microsoft Word documents or even Powerpoint presentations • Rendered output uses real semantic headings, lists, tables, links, and landmarks — so what you share is accessible to whoever receives it Your Files, Your Devices: • Documents are ordinary Markdown files, visible in the Files app • Store them on your device, or turn on iCloud Drive to sync across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac • Open and edit the same files in any other app that reads text • Nothing is locked in a proprietary format, and nothing needs this app to survive Accessibility: Developed toward WCAG 2.2 Level AA and tested with VoiceOver as a primary interaction method. • A predictable, linear VoiceOver reading order • Native controls with the roles and behaviors you already expect • Dynamic Type, including accessibility text sizes, everywhere • System, monospaced, rounded, and serif editor typefaces • Light, dark, and system appearance • Voice Control, Switch Control, and hardware keyboard support • Optional keyboard shortcuts for common actions • Reduced-motion support Privacy: No accounts. No sign-in. No ads. No analytics. No tracking. No data collection of any kind. There is no server behind this app because there doesn't need to be one. Your documents are yours, on your device or in your own iCloud, and they never travel anywhere you don't send them. Made by a blind developer who got tired of using tools that treated screen reader support as an afterthought. Heading

title: Intersector: Intersection Identifier
summary: Hear your upcoming intersections while walking, when in a rideshare, or on a bus with the new Live Mode. Intersector helps you quickly identify nearby street intersections using your iPhone’s location and heading. Ask for the nearest intersection, what’s coming up ahead, use Scan Mode to point your phone down the street and hear the intersection it detects, or turn on Live Mode and have Intersector speak your upcoming intersections on a walk or during a ride with your phone locked. Intersector can speak distance, direction, and neighborhood context, and includes optional wording styles so announcements can match how you think about your surroundings. Built with VoiceOver users in mind, Intersector focuses on fast, clear spoken information without turning into turn-by-turn navigation. It is designed as a lightweight orientation tool for understanding nearby cross streets, not as a crossing aid or safety system. Features include: • Nearest intersection announcements • Upcoming intersection announcements • Scan Mode for nearby intersections in the direction you point • Live Mode to announce upcoming intersections automatically while walking or in transportation, using customizable speech • Siri Shortcut support • Optional distance, direction, and neighborhood details • Customizable intersection wording • Support for split intersections where different streets meet the same main street • Manhattan Snob Mode for New York-style direction wording • VoiceOver-friendly controls and spoken feedback • Dynamic Type and large text support. Intersector also has an Apple Watch companion app, so Siri Shortcuts and intersection data can be queried right from your wrist. Intersector uses location and heading data to provide orientation information. Always use your own judgment, mobility skills, and available pedestrian infrastructure when traveling.
